claims.text: No localized finding on exam: X-rays of both lower extremities.
claims.quote: In a child with a limp and no localized pathology on clinical examination, plain radiography of both lower extremities should be performed.

claims.text: Localized finding: AP and lateral X-rays of that area.
claims.quote: If localized pathology is suggested on clinical examination, anteroposterior and lateral radiography of the affected areas should be performed.

claims.text: Hip effusion: ultrasound rather than plain X-ray.
claims.quote: Ultrasonography is recommended over plain radiography for detecting hip effusions because of its high sensitivity.

claims.text: Suspected infection, inflammatory arthritis or tumor: CBC with differential, ESR and CRP; aspirate the joint urgently (Gram stain, culture, cell count) if septic arthritis is suspected.
claims.quote: A complete blood count with differential, erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) measurement should be obtained when infection, inflammatory arthritis, or neoplasm is suspected. If septic arthritis is suspected, joint fluid aspiration should be performed urgently for Gram staining, culture, and cell count.

claims.text: Septic arthritis over transient synovitis is more likely with temperature > 38.5°C, refusal to bear weight, ESR > 40 mm/h, WBC > 12,000/mm3 or CRP > 20 mg/L.
claims.quote: The following clinical features make septic arthritis more likely than transient synovitis: oral temperature more than 101.3°F (38.5°C), refusal to bear weight on the affected leg, erythrocyte sedimentation rate more than 40 mm per hour, peripheral white blood cell count more than 12,000 per mm 3 (12 × 10 9 per L), or C-reactive protein level more than 20 mg per L (180.96 nmol per L).
